claims.text: Adding 2 at.% boron to an as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy will form boride precipitates.
Precipitate-induced restriction of dislocation mobility will increase alloy strength.
Adding 2 at.% boron will improve high-temperature yield strength by 15% relative to the as-cast alloy without boron.
The proposed high-temperature strength improvement will hold over 800-1000°C and applied loads of 100-500 MPa.
Adding 2 at.% boron will increase density by less than 1%.
Adding 2 at.% boron will cause no significant change in room-temperature performance.
Precipitation strengthening is a viable strategy for improving elevated-temperature strength in high-entropy alloys.
The amount of boron and the resulting microstructure may affect the outcome.
The formation of borides and their effect on dislocation mobility in the proposed alloy are not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires a 15% strength improvement, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below 10%; a result from 10% to under 15% would contradict the prediction without meeting the stated falsification rule.

The prediction limits density increase to less than 1%, but falsification occurs only above 2%; an increase from 1% through 2% would violate the prediction without falsifying it under the stated rule.
Preservation of room-temperature performance is part of the hypothesis, but the proposed measurements contain no room-temperature mechanical test, so this component cannot be decisively assessed.
